create-project.title: Create a Project
create-project.description: Template for setting up a new Project in claude.ai
create-project.text:
Help me set up a new Project in claude.ai for my task.

Context:
- Topic / domain: [fill in yours]
- Who I am: [role]
- Audience for responses: [who I'm using it for]

Generate for the Project:
1. Name (short, clear).
2. Description (1-2 sentences).
3. Custom Instructions:
   - Claude's role
   - response style (length, format, tone)
   - 3-5 rules / taboos
   - output format for a typical request
4. List of 5 files / documents worth uploading to the project.
5. Example first request to verify everything works.

Response format: sections with headings, no fluff.

create-artifact.title: Create an Artifact
create-artifact.description: A solid interactive prototype with a single prompt
create-artifact.text:
Make an interactive Artifact (HTML + Tailwind, no external libraries).

What we're building: [prototype description — e.g.: input form, dashboard, comparison screen]
Audience: [who will use it]
Device: mobile-first, but correct on desktop.

Requirements:
- semantic HTML
- Tailwind CSS via CDN
- interactivity via native JS (no React/Vue)
- baseline accessibility: aria-label, contrast ≥ 4.5:1, focus
- 2-3 states (idle, loading, success / error)
- comments in code only where logic is non-obvious

Show a preview so I can check immediately.

create-skill.title: Create a Skill
create-skill.text:
Create a Skill for a recurring task.

Task: [describe the recurring process]
When to trigger: [keywords or situations]
What Claude should do: [step by step]

Generate:
1. SKILL.md:
   - name (kebab-case)
   - description (so Claude knows exactly when to activate — concrete triggers)
   - role / context
   - step-by-step workflow (5-8 steps)
   - final output format
2. templates/output.md — final answer template.
3. Input example and output example.
4. 3 situations where the Skill should NOT activate (anti-triggers).

The key thing — a precise description; activation depends on it.

create-claudemd.title: Create CLAUDE.md
create-claudemd.description: Project instructions file for Claude Code
create-claudemd.text:
Generate CLAUDE.md for my project.

Stack: [languages, frameworks, libraries]
Project type: [web-app / CLI / library / monorepo]
Team: [solo / 2-5 / more]

Include sections:
1. Brief about the project (2-3 lines) — only what's non-obvious from package.json.
2. Stack and versions.
3. Code conventions: naming, folder structure, imports.
4. Testing: framework, how to run, coverage requirements.
5. Linting and formatting: commands, rules.
6. Forbidden (taboos): patterns, libraries, approaches.
7. Entry points: key files and their purpose.
8. Links to external systems (issue tracker, docs, design tools) — if any.

Style: terse, no fluff. Only what Claude can't figure out from the code itself.

expert-audit.title: Run an expert audit
expert-audit.description: Deep audit of your material against a checklist
expert-audit.text:
Run an expert audit on the material.

What we're auditing: [document / screen / process / code — whatever you have]
Material's goal: [what it should do or show]
Audience: [whom it's for]
Domain: [where you work — product / marketing / development / process / other]

Checklist (adapt items to your domain):
1. Structure and hierarchy: what's scannable in 5 seconds.
2. Key action / goal: clarity, wording, visibility.
3. Accessibility / clarity: for the target audience without preparation.
4. User load: number of fields / steps / decisions.
5. Trust: confirmations, sources, transparency.
6. Robustness: what breaks under awkward conditions.
7. Performance / efficiency: how quickly the outcome is reached.
8. Risks: where you can lose a user / outcome.

Output format (for each issue):
- What: [one line]
- Impact: [high / medium / low + why]
- Recommendation: [concrete action]

At the end — top-5 actions by priority.

html-prototype.title: Create an HTML prototype
html-prototype.description: Prototype in pure HTML/CSS, ready to review
html-prototype.text:
Make an HTML prototype in a single file.

What: [e.g. onboarding screen]
Scenario: [what the user does step by step]
Tone: [strict B2B / friendly B2C / minimal]

Technical requirements:
- one index.html — nothing external besides Tailwind CDN
- three states (where applicable): empty, filled, error
- mobile-first, breaks gracefully down to 320px
- accessible semantics: label, aria-*, hidden descriptions
- no lorem ipsum — write meaningful placeholder text
- comments in HTML only when doing something non-trivial

Format as an Artifact so I can open the preview.

consistency-audit.title: Consistency audit
consistency-audit.description: Find duplicates, anomalies and discrepancies in a system
consistency-audit.text:
Check the system's consistency.

What system: [e.g.: design system, code library, document templates, content style, processes]
Sources: [links to files / repository / description]
What matters now: [concrete aspect — pick 2-3 most important]

Check:
1. Base units (colors / variables / terms / templates): duplicates, shades, usage outside the standard.
2. Sizes and parameters: number of variants; any «magic» values.
3. Structure and grid: alignment with the accepted system; anomalies.
4. Repeating elements with different implementations.
5. Accessibility / clarity for the target audience.
6. Naming: consistency, clarity.

For each finding:
- What
- Where (file / section / component)
- Severity
- What to do

At the end — top-3 systemic problems (not pointwise).

dev-task.title: Prepare a task for a developer
dev-task.description: User story with AC, risks and an estimate
dev-task.text:
Turn an idea into a task for a developer.

Idea: [short description]
Business context: [why this is needed]
Constraints: [deadlines, stack, dependencies]

Generate:
1. User story (As a … I want … so that …).
2. Acceptance Criteria — Given/When/Then, 4-7 items.
3. Technical notes: what we touch, what we do NOT touch.
4. Edge cases and negative scenarios.
5. Risks and blockers.
6. Dependencies (other tickets, teams).
7. Size estimate (XS/S/M/L/XL) with rationale.
8. Definition of Done.

Format: markdown, ready to paste into your task tracker.

create-agent.title: Create an agent
create-agent.description: Subagent in Claude Code for a recurring task
create-agent.text:
Make a spec for a new Subagent in Claude Code.

Agent's goal: [what it does]
When to call: [triggers from the user's prompt]
Tool access: [Read / Edit / Bash / Web... — what's needed, no more]

Describe:
1. Name (kebab-case).
2. Description — so the parent agent knows when to delegate.
3. System prompt (role, context, constraints).
4. Workflow: step by step, what the agent does.
5. Report format to the parent (short, structured).
6. Anti-patterns: what the agent does NOT do.
7. Example of a good call and a bad call.

The key thing — description; it decides whether the agent activates.

improve-prompt.title: Improve a prompt
improve-prompt.description: Turn a weak request into a working one
improve-prompt.text:
Improve my prompt.

My current prompt:
"""
[paste here]
"""

What I want as output:
[describe the ideal answer]

Do:
1. Diagnostic: what's weak in the current prompt (context / role / task / format / constraints).
2. Rewrite the prompt by structure: context → role → task → format → constraints → example.
3. Add 1-2 Few-shot examples if they help.
4. Explain what changes you made and why.
5. Provide a «short» version (1 paragraph) and a «full» one (structured).

Goal — the same request with an improved prompt consistently yields a higher-quality answer.
